question: Látka taurín, ktorú nájdete na plechovke takmer každého energetického nápoja, má meno odvodené z latinčiny. Podľa ktorého zvieraťa ju pomenovali?
source_excerpt: The name taurine is derived from Latin taurus (cognate to Ancient Greek ταῦρος, taûros) meaning bull or ox, as it was first isolated from ox bile in 1827.

extra.why_interesting: Players see 'taurín' on every can in Slovak shops but never connect it to the zodiac sign Býk (Taurus). Once they make the link they can reason it out, and then they learn the bull legend is real but the drink contains no animal at all.
extra.verification_notes: Taurine is named from Latin taurus (bull/ox) because it was first isolated from ox bile, per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taurine.

explanation: Latinské „taurus“ znamená býk, rovnako ako znamenie Býka vo zverokruhu. Prvýkrát ho vedci získali z volskej žlče, no taurín v plechovkách sa dnes vyrába synteticky a so zvieratami nemá nič spoločné.

question: Red Bull je rakúska značka, ale jeho recept aj logo s dvoma býkmi sú prevzaté z lacného nápoja pre ázijských robotníkov a vodičov kamiónov. Z ktorej krajiny pochádza pôvodný nápoj?
source_excerpt: Thai entrepreneur Chaleo Yoovidhya introduced a similar drink, Krating Daeng, in 1976. Austrian Dietrich Mateschitz found it helped his jet lag and co-founded Red Bull GmbH

extra.why_interesting: Slovaks see Red Bull as an Austrian brand from next door, tied to Alps and Formula 1. They don't expect it to be a remake of a cheap Asian drink for truckers. The stem's mention of Asia narrows the options to a reasoning game, and the logo explanation adds a satisfying 'aha'.
extra.verification_notes: Red Bull derives from Thailand's Krating Daeng (Chaleo Yoovidhya, 1976), per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Bull; no newer event changes this.

explanation: Rakúšan Dietrich Mateschitz objavil v Thajsku nápoj Krating Daeng, čo znamená „červený gaur“, teda divý ázijský tur. Ten upravil pre európsky vkus a doslova preložil aj jeho názov.
